lines: A blinded randomized trial compares assignment to active treatment versus placebo on mean symptom change atWeek12,100participants per group.

AllWeek12values were measured. The unadjusted analysis discards measured values after treatment stopping:20active participants stopped because symptoms worsened;2placebo stopped for administrative reasons. Remaining values retain randomized grouping.

One active participant used rescue treatment; its data were also excluded. The reported favorable active mean is computed from retained observations. Omitted active values show markedly worse symptom changes than retained active values; no prognostic or censoring adjustment is used.
cases.review: Restriction on measured outcomes selects unfavorable active outcomes; single rescue does not settle other restriction. Supported probable substantial impact, without needing a formal numerical bound.

lines: A blinded randomized trial compares assignment to active treatment versus placebo on mean symptom change atWeek12,100participants per group.

AllWeek12values were measured. The unadjusted analysis discards measured values for two administrative treatment stops in each group; these values and baseline prognosis resemble the retained values. Remaining values retain randomized grouping.
The report also gives the all-randomized analysis retaining those measurements: its effect estimate and confidence interval are practically unchanged, with no other restrictions.
cases.review: Measured-value restriction is inappropriate for assignment; positive source-supported robustness and prognosis permit probable negligible impact, not NI merely because stopping occurred.

lines: A blinded randomized trial compares assignment to active treatment versus placebo on mean symptom change atWeek12,100participants per group.

The report calls the analysis ITT but states efficacy observations were censored after treatment stopping;18active and9placebo participants stopped. It does not say whether subsequent values were measured or unavailable.
Stopping reasons, post-stop symptoms and the analysis assumptions for those observations are not available. No outcome or prognostic comparison of affected participants is reported.
cases.review: Known rule and stopping counts do not establish recorded-value omission or outcome-dependent loss. Unresolved mechanism/outcomes allow honest NI; no small-count shortcut or fabricated bias certainty.

lines: A blinded randomized trial compares assignment to active treatment versus placebo on mean symptom change atWeek12,100participants per group.
Twentyactive andtenplacebo participants stopped treatment, but allWeek12values were measured and retained in the all-randomized analysis by assigned group.
No adherence restriction, wrong-group analysis or other exclusion occurred.
cases.review: Stopping alone is not analysis bias;2.6appropriate and2.7inactive.
